title: Empty Report Explained
pageTitle: Empty Report Explained · a sample incident walkthrough
description: A made-up incident, explained step by step: why a nightly report came out empty and how the fix was proven.
subject: Nightly sales report, Mar 9

intro.heading: Why was the nightly report empty?
intro.lead: The clocks moved forward an hour, so the report ran before the export finished. The fix makes the report wait for the export.
facts: copies the day's sales into the warehouse
reads the warehouse and emails a summary
a clock that never changes for daylight saving
a row the export writes when it finishes

guess.title: Best explanation, not observed
guess.text: The logs show the timing. Nobody saw the scheduler skip a check; that part is inferred.

footer: Made-up example for the incident preset. Names, times and numbers are illustrative.

lessons.name: An empty email
lessons.summary: The report ran, found no rows for the day, and emailed a summary of zero sales.

steps.title: Start
steps.desc: At 02:00 UTC the scheduler starts the report.

msgs.what: Tells the report job to begin its run at 02:00 UTC.
msgs.why: The scheduler starts the report at a set clock time. It does not check whether the export has finished.

steps.title: Query
steps.desc: The report asks for yesterday's sales and gets nothing back.

msgs.what: Requests the warehouse's sales rows for the previous day.
msgs.why: The summary is built from these rows. Without them the report has nothing to total.

msgs.what: Returns an empty result: no sales rows for the date.
msgs.why: The export had not loaded the day's sales yet. The report treated the empty result as real and carried on.

steps.title: Send
steps.desc: It emails a summary anyway: zero sales.

msgs.what: Emails the sales team a summary showing a total of $0.
msgs.why: This is the symptom people saw. The report treated zero rows as a real total, so it sent a wrong summary.

lessons.name: Export first, then report
lessons.summary: The export finishes around 01:40 UTC. The report starts at 02:00 UTC, so the data is always there.

steps.title: Load
steps.desc: The export writes the day's sales.

msgs.what: Loads the day's 4,812 sales rows into the warehouse, finishing about 01:40 UTC.
msgs.why: The report can only total what is already there. Finishing first leaves a 20-minute margin before 02:00 UTC.

steps.title: Read
steps.desc: Twenty minutes later the report reads them.

msgs.what: Asks the warehouse for the day's sales at 02:00 UTC.
msgs.why: The export is done by now, so the data is ready. This read is the healthy path.

msgs.what: Returns all 4,812 rows the export loaded.
msgs.why: The report gets a full day of data to summarise, so the email is correct.

lessons.name: The clocks moved
lessons.summary: Daylight saving started. The export follows local time, so it ran an hour later in UTC. The report follows UTC, so it didn't move.

steps.title: Early
steps.desc: The report reads first and finds nothing.

msgs.what: Asks for the day's sales at 02:00 UTC, the same query as on a normal night.
msgs.why: The schedule did not move with the clocks, so this runs before the export has loaded anything.

msgs.what: Returns zero rows because the export has not written yet.
msgs.why: The report needs the day's rows to build its email. With none there yet, the email went out empty. Best explanation, not observed.

steps.title: Late
steps.desc: The export lands 40 minutes later, too late for the email.

msgs.what: Writes 4,790 rows at 02:40 UTC, 40 minutes after the report had already read.
msgs.why: Daylight saving pushed the local-time export an hour later in UTC. The data is fine but too late for the email.

lessons.name: Wait for the done flag
lessons.summary: Use the Before and After buttons. After the fix, the report waits for the export's done flag instead of a fixed time.
facts: start on done flag, not on the clock

steps.title: Guess
steps.desc: The report starts at 02:00 UTC whether or not the data is there.

msgs.what: Reads the warehouse at a fixed 02:00 UTC with no check that the data exists.
msgs.why: A clock time is a guess about when the export finishes. When the export moves, the guess is wrong.

steps.title: Flag
steps.desc: The export writes a done row when it finishes.

msgs.what: Writes a done row for Mar 9 once the export finishes.
msgs.why: It gives the report a signal that the data is complete, so the report does not rely on the time.

steps.title: Read
steps.desc: The report checks for the flag, then reads.

msgs.what: Asks whether the done flag for the day exists.
msgs.why: The report waits for the flag, so it never reads before the data is there.

msgs.what: Confirms the flag is set and returns 4,790 rows.
msgs.why: With the flag set, the report reads the full data. The Mar 9 rerun produced 4,790 rows.

lessons.name: Watch the autumn change
lessons.summary: The fix should hold when the clocks move back too, but that hasn't happened yet.

aside.text: The first autumn run after the fix is the real test.

steps.title: Next
steps.desc: Check the first report after the clocks move back.

msgs.what: Starts the first report after the clocks move back, to see whether the fix holds.
msgs.why: The fix is untested for the autumn change. This run is the real test, so it is marked not verified.
